Hi Elaine — quick technical replies inline below. Pulling together short snippets and config you can paste into your SDK layer.

Q: sync vs async for embeddings + reranker at sub-200ms SLA
A: If you require sub-200ms 95p, we typically recommend the async hybrid pattern: compute query embedding inline, then hit a fast nearest-neighbor index (hosted or self-managed) for candidate retrieval, then call the reranker as a separate (very low-latency) scoring RPC. That avoids blocking on heavier model reranker loads and lets you parallelize retrieval vs rerank. If you want fully sync, use a dedicated small-capacity reranker pool pinned to your account (Redwood Dedicated) to meet latency SLOs.

Q: headers for 429/backoff
A: Redwood returns standard Retry-After when the server has a target backoff window. However, for transient throttles we sometimes return a 429 without Retry-After to avoid exposing internal pacing; in that case use an exponential backoff with full jitter. Suggested client policy: initial delay = 100ms, multiplier = 2, max delay = 5s, max attempts = 5. Respect Retry-After if present.

Q: X-Request-ID and idempotency
A: X-Request-ID is useful for tracing but by itself does not imply idempotency for all endpoints. For stateful operations (e.g., upserts, billing-affecting calls) pass an Idempotency-Key header. For stateless scoring/reranker calls, we treat repeated identical requests as side-effect-free (scores only) and do not dedupe; however, you can still set X-Request-ID so we surface debug traces and avoid duplicate billing if a retry is reprocessed within a short window.

SDK sample (pseudocode):
- Headers: { Authorization: "Bearer <token>", "X-Request-ID": "{uuid}", "Idempotency-Key": "{optional-id}" }
- Timeout: connect=50ms, read=1500ms (adjust for region)
- Retry policy: attempt up to 5 times for 5xx/429; treat 4xx other than 429 as terminal.

Routing / regional latency
- You can set a region hint in the request (region=us-east-1) or we will route by geo-ip. For strict regional routing use the dedicated VPC/private option.

Structured output & tool-calling
- For function/tool calling we recommend using the structured-output endpoint with a schema. If you expect retries, design your tool calls to be idempotent or make the tool side reconcile on receipt (e.g., upsert semantics).
